# Rebuilding with build.sh

This page is for developers who changed a package folder and need the `.ezpkg` archive the installer downloads. It
explains the two packing scripts of the 7x source repositories, what ends up in an archive, and how to check the
result before anyone else gets it.

7x and the Exponential Foundation strongly encourage you to submit the archives you build by pull request to
se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth: see [Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).

## Contents

1. [What an .ezpkg archive is](#what-an-ezpkg-archive-is)
2. [packages/build.sh](#packagesbuildsh)
3. [bin/pack.sh](#binpacksh)
4. [Check the archive](#check-the-archive)

## What an .ezpkg archive is

A gzip-compressed tar archive of one package folder, with `package.xml` at its top (not inside a folder named after
the package). The kernel checks exactly that on import: the file starts with the gzip signature, every entry is a plain
file or a directory with a relative path, and `package.xml` is at the top
(`kernel/classes/ezpackageuploadinspector.php`). More on [The .ezpkg file](../basics/the-ezpkg-file.md).

## packages/build.sh

The script of [se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage](https://github.com/se7enxweb/sevenx-ezpackage), run from inside `packages/`:

```bash
cd packages
bash build.sh
ls *.ezpkg
```

What it does, in order:

1. Loops over every entry of the current directory (`for folder in *`).
2. Skips anything that is not a directory, so the `.ezpkg` files of an earlier run and `build.sh` itself are left
   alone.
3. Changes into the folder and runs `tar -zcf ../<folder>.ezpkg <excludes> *`: the archive is named after the
   folder and written next to it, and `*` puts the folder's contents at the top of the archive.

The excludes, as the script lists them:

| Left out | Why |
|---|---|
| `.git`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `.gitmodules`, `.svn`, `.hg` | version control files of bundled extension working copies |
| `.DS_Store`, `.idea`, `.vscode` | operating system and editor folders |
| `*~`, `*.swp` | editor backups and swap files |
| `node_modules` | build dependencies |

tar applies each name at any depth. Everything else in the folder goes in, including files a script or an editor
left beside the XML files. Look at `git status` and the folder before you build.

> **Note**
> `*` does not match names that start with a dot at the top of the folder, so a top-level dot file is never packed;
> the excludes cover the ones deeper down.

## bin/pack.sh

The older script, also in `cjw_multisite-ezpackage` (which has no `packages/build.sh`). Run it from the repository root:

```bash
bash bin/pack.sh --output-dir="$PWD/build"
```

The script uses the `function` keyword, which bash understands and some `/bin/sh` shells do not, so call it with
`bash`. It changes into `packages/` before packing, so give `--output-dir` as an absolute path.

It walks `packages/`, skips a folder named `package_set`, and writes `<output-dir>/<folder>.ezpkg` with the same
excludes plus `.cache` and `pack_and_publish.bat`. Without `--output-dir` it writes to a fixed default folder under
`/tmp`; always pass the option so the archives land where you expect them.

`ant/createzpkg.sh <source> <destination>` packs a single folder (excluding `.svn`, `.cache`,
`pack_and_publish.bat`), and `bin/repack_extension.sh` rebuilds an extension package with `ezpm`
([Creating packages with ezpm](creating-packages-with-ezpm.md)).

## Check the archive

```bash
# the top of the archive: package.xml first-level, no wrapping folder
tar -tzf acme_site.ezpkg | head

# the gzip signature the importer checks (1f 8b)
head -c 2 acme_site.ezpkg | od -An -tx1

# the definition is well formed
tar -xzOf acme_site.ezpkg package.xml | xmllint --noout -

# the kernel's own check, without importing (in an installation)
php ezpm.php validate /path/to/acme_site.ezpkg
```

`ezpm validate` accepts an archive, a package directory or a package name and checks every document, the definition
as the kernel reads it, the documents the items name and, for JSON packages, the schema and checksums. The limits an
upload must stay under (`package.ini [UploadSettings]`: 256 MiB per archive, 2 GiB unpacked, 50000 entries by default)
are on [Validating a package before publishing](../requirements/validating-a-package-before-publishing.md).

## Compare with the previous release

A rebuild of an unchanged folder is not byte-identical (tar records times), so compare the lists, not the files:

```bash
diff <(tar -tzf old/acme_site.ezpkg | sort) <(tar -tzf acme_site.ezpkg | sort)
```

Every line of the difference should be explained by a commit since the last release.

## From archive to package server

The 7x release process, as it applies to any package server:

1. Change the package in the source repository and commit.
2. Run `packages/build.sh`.
3. Compare the new archives with the published ones.
4. Copy each `.ezpkg` into the package server repository under `exponential/6.0/<version>/`.
5. Update that folder's `index.xml` (and `thumbnails/` for a new site package).
6. Commit and push; the server republishes ([How a release reaches the package server](../package-server/how-a-release-reaches-the-package-server.md)).

For your own server see [Running your own package server](running-your-own-package-server.md).
